title: 《发哨子的人》：刊载、失去可见性、文本变体与记忆幸存的初步来源登记
methodological_warning: Published page metadata, cached reprints, journalist descriptions of unavailability, and original-platform evidence are distinct. No original WeChat article URL or verified bytes of its 2020-03-10 first edition are established. nCovMemory CSV row 3142 records a candidate original WeChat URL and archive link but their original content remains unverified.

privacy: No copied unredacted chat logs, patients' reports, private family identifiers or full copyrighted interview text. Public URLs only; no private screenshots.
originality_boundary:
Sun & Wright (2023 online, 2024 issue) already study relay activism on WeChat/GitHub. The current pilot asks which platform/edition and secondary-journalism claims are independently authenticatable, particularly the eight-person police-label conflation across cases. Wu (2024) also identifies textual, multimodal and technically encoded relay tactics. Avoid repackaging these findings; prioritize source-version attestation and labeled-actor conflation with cross-case corrections. Source discovery: known WeChat URL improves targeted authentication but does not establish exact original text. A concrete March 10 Git commit chain goes back to 13:23:09 Beijing time on a predecessor Chinese filename. Only 73/75 normalized long paragraphs are identical across first and last reviewed editions (remaining: metadata and one
formatting difference). The first copy contains the 'eight admonished doctors' editorial summary twice but the 'I was not admonished by police' self-report once; avoid counting these as three independent statements. A directly accessible Wayback capture at 2020-03-10T13:50:52Z preserves a March10 institutional reprint on yyrw.org.cn with materially different framing/credit; this is verified archived content, not original WeChat edition. A distinct archive.today locator 20200310021029 appears in secondary bibliography but target is inaccessible; do not backdate content to it. Concrete frame inversion now observed: first Git copy '发哨子的人', 21:50 archived professional association repost '吹哨子的人', while first-person testimony distinguishes the terms. Also byline role flattening and an additional opening sentence. No motive attribution. New reported directive evidence explicitly references the same institutionally reprinted yyrw.org.cn URL; critically distinguish Feb7 terminology prohibition, Mar10 homepage placement restriction, delayed public leak and actually observable site removal. CDTs 2020 alleged central instructions and 2026 LeTV internal catalog have a common passage, not independently proven issuer lineages.
